doc: OpenTelemetry's Google Gen AI instrumentation, which serves both the Gemini Developer API and Vertex AI modes of the `google-genai` client. Identity lives in `vertex-ai.json`; this asset holds the instrumentation's own message shapes.

carriers.doc: The arguments an `execute_tool` span was handed, read from its flattened `code.function.parameters` family: the span's input, like the conventions' arguments attribute.
That span's own result in the same releases: one emission, as the conventions' result attribute is.

content_blocks.doc: An inline image or document. The semantic conventions' BlobPart holds its bytes, base64-encoded, under `content` beside `mime_type` and `modality`; this instrumentation writes it without the `type` member, so it reached no media reading and was kept as an unknown block.

messages.doc: A function the client called itself, recorded on its `execute_tool` span. The instrumentation writes each argument as `code.function.parameters.<name>.value` beside its Python type, so the arguments the model sent are those members, not the object; read as written, the call matched no copy of itself on the model span and appeared twice. Arguments in any other shape fall through to the semantic-conventions rule. Releases before 1.1 emit the same spans through OpenTelemetry's shared GenAI handler, under that handler's scope.

The same call as written by releases before 0.8, which put each argument on the `execute_tool` span itself as `code.function.parameters.<name>.value` instead of in `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments`. The family is read as one object and the `.value` members are the arguments.

Its result in those releases: `code.function.return.value`, the function's return value as JSON text or a plain string, on the same span. A `tool_result` block named like the semantic-conventions result.
